state.task:
Define SLO for checkout API
The product team wants an SLO for the checkout API. Read ops/dashboards/checkout.json and the incidents list in docs/incidents/2026.md. Propose one availability SLO and one latency SLO with the measurement window and the error budget. Keep the answer under twenty lines.

Assess correctness of distributed lock
The job scheduler in C:/work/scheduler uses a Redis lock in locks/redis_lock.py to make sure only one worker runs the nightly settlement job. The lock is taken with SET key value NX PX 30000 and released with a Lua script that compares the token. Recently two workers ran settlement at the same time, and some ledger rows were written twice.

Task: decide whether the lock implementation is the cause, and if it is not, identify the real cause. Read locks/redis_lock.py, workers/settlement.py and the config in config/scheduler.yaml. Note the lock TTL of 30 seconds and the job duration, which the log logs/settlement_2026_11_03.log shows is 41 to 47 seconds on large days. Check whether the job renews the lock, and if it does, check the renewal interval and whether the renewal runs in a separate thread that can outlive the job.

Consider the classic failure where a process pauses longer than the TTL, for example during a garbage collection pause or a long database call, then resumes and believes it still holds the lock. Check whether the fencing token is passed to the database writes. Check whether ledger writes include the lock token as a condition, or whether they rely only on the lock being held.

Also check the retry logic in workers/settlement.py for a case where a failed acquire is retried immediately, and whether the scheduler starts the job on a second node after a health check timeout.

Constraints: do not change the lock code in this task. Do not write to the Redis instance; read only commands are fine if you have a sandbox, but you should not need one. Do not modify the ledger table.

Report back: whether the lock is the cause (yes or no) with evidence, the timeline of the two runs reconstructed from the log with timestamps, the smallest code change that would make double writes impossible even when the lock expires, and a list of the files and lines that the change would touch. Keep the report under 40 lines.

Diagnose intermittent 502 on deploy
During rolling deploys about one in twenty requests returns 502 from the nginx ingress for roughly 3 seconds. The app is gunicorn with uvicorn workers configured in deploy/gunicorn.conf.py. Read deploy/gunicorn.conf.py, deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml and the log excerpt in logs/deploy_2026_11_01.txt. Form hypotheses about the graceful shutdown timeout, the readiness probe and the keep-alive setting. Rank them by evidence. Propose one experiment to confirm the top one. Do not change the deployment files.

Investigate JWT validation flaw
A security review flagged a possible issue in the auth service at services/auth/src/jwt/verify.ts. The reviewer says a token signed with the none algorithm might be accepted under some configuration. Investigate the code paths and report the findings. Do not patch the code in this task, and do not write an exploit against any running environment.
Read verify.ts and the config loader in services/auth/src/config.ts. Check how the algorithm list is set, whether it defaults to an empty list, and whether the verify call passes algorithms explicitly. Check whether the library version in package-lock.json is one where the jsonwebtoken package requires an explicit algorithms option. Read the test file services/auth/test/verify.test.ts and list which algorithm cases it covers.
Also check whether the audience and issuer claims are checked, and whether the clock tolerance is set to a value that allows long-expired tokens. Search the repo for any other call to jwt.decode, which skips signature checks, and list each use with file and line. Decoding is fine for logging only, so flag any use where its result drives an authorization decision.
Write a short finding list in .agent/scratch.md with each finding, its severity as low, medium, or high, and the exact evidence.
Report back with: the findings in severity order, each with its file and line, the algorithm configuration you found, the test coverage gaps, the jwt.decode uses that drive authorization, and whether you could confirm the none algorithm path from the code alone.

Design a plugin loader interface
The reporting service needs third-party report plugins. Propose a small Java interface for loading plugins from a folder of jars, with versioning and failure isolation. Do not write the implementation. Give the interface signature, the failure rules, and two open questions for the team in under twenty lines.

Assess Redis cache stampede risk
The product catalog cache in catalog/cache.py uses a fixed TTL of 60 seconds per key. During a promotion one key expired and about 800 requests hit the database within two seconds. Assess the stampede risk. Compare lock-based recompute, probabilistic early expiration and stale-while-revalidate. Recommend one approach for this code and sketch the code change in at most 15 lines in your report. Do not edit files.

Find race in job scheduler lease
Two workers sometimes run the same job in internal/scheduler. Reproduce with the test in internal/scheduler/lease_stress_test.go. Find the race window and report the fix options with their trade-offs. Do not edit the scheduler yet.

Decide consistency model for inventory
The inventory service in C:/work/stock-platform handles reservations for online orders across three warehouses. Users see overselling about once per thousand orders during flash sales. The service uses PostgreSQL with a stock table per warehouse and a reservation table. The writes happen in services/reserve.py, the read path that shows availability is in services/availability.py, and the cache for availability sits in cache/avail.py with a TTL of 20 seconds.

Task: choose the consistency approach for reservations. Read the three service files, docs/inventory/requirements.md and the incident notes in docs/inventory/incidents_2026.md. Compare these options: a row lock with SELECT FOR UPDATE on the stock row, an optimistic version column with retry, a single atomic UPDATE with a check constraint, and a reservation queue processed by one worker per warehouse. For each option, describe the behavior under flash sale load of 2000 orders per second for ten seconds on a single hot SKU, the expected p99 latency, the failure modes including deadlocks and lost updates, and how the availability cache affects the answer.

The availability cache returns stale numbers for up to 20 seconds. Decide whether a reservation may trust the cache at all. Decide what the user sees when the reservation fails after the cache said the item was available.

Address operational concerns: which option needs the least new code, how to roll out without downtime, how to monitor oversell events, and how to reconcile after an incident.

Constraints: do not modify code or schema. Do not run load tests against any shared database. Any benchmark estimate must be labeled as an estimate with its assumptions listed.

Deliver a decision memo of at most 100 lines written to docs/decisions/inventory_consistency.md, with a recommendation at the top and a table comparing the options. Include the open questions for the operations team at the end.

Report back: the path of the memo, the recommended option in one sentence, the main risk of that option in one sentence, and the open questions. Keep the report under 25 lines.

Design versioned API rollout
A public REST API must add a breaking change next quarter. Read docs/api/policy.md and the current routes in services/public-api/routes. Propose the versioning scheme and the sunset steps. Keep under twenty lines. Do not write code.

Resolve conflicting business rules in pricing
The pricing engine in C:/work/pricing-engine has three rules that conflict for members buying bundles. The rule files are rules/member_discount.yaml, rules/bundle_discount.yaml and rules/promo_cap.yaml. Member discount gives 10 percent off every item. Bundle discount gives 15 percent off a bundle of three or more items from the same brand. The promo cap says the total discount on one order may not exceed 20 percent of the list price. Members who buy a bundle now sometimes get 25 percent off, which violates the cap, and sometimes the cap is applied in a way that gives less discount than the rules promise.

Task: determine what the correct behavior should be and where the code violates it. Read rules/*.yaml, pricing/engine.py and pricing/apply.py. Read docs/pricing/policy_2026.md, which is the business policy document, and find the section that describes stacking. Read tests/pricing/test_stacking.py to see what the tests currently assert.

Work through three example carts by hand and write the expected totals. Cart A: a member buys three items of brand X at 40 each, total list 120. Cart B: a member buys four items of brand X at 25 and one item of brand Y at 100, total list 200. Cart C: a non member buys three items of brand X at 40. Compute the totals under the policy text, then under the code, using a short script in your scratch folder if needed, and report both numbers for each cart.

Identify the order in which the engine applies discounts, and whether the cap is applied to the discount sum or to each step. Check whether the engine applies the member discount to the already reduced bundle price. Explain which of the two orders the policy intends.

Constraints: do not change rules or code. Do not change the policy document. If the policy is ambiguous, list the ambiguity and do not pick one silently; state the two readings and their totals.

Report back: the correct behavior per the policy with a citation to the section, the expected and actual totals for Carts A, B and C, the file and line where the order of application is set, and the questions the business owner must answer before a fix. Keep the report under 40 lines.

Audit background job idempotency
Several background jobs in jobs/ are not idempotent. For example jobs/send_reminders.py sends an email each time it runs for a given booking, and jobs/close_periods.py may close a period twice. Read the five job modules in jobs/ and identify each non-idempotent side effect with file and line. Rank them by business impact. For the top two, propose the smallest guard, such as a unique constraint or a processed-marker table. Do not edit code.

Split monolithic Terraform root
The Terraform root directory infra/root contains networking, databases, and application deployment in one state. The plan now takes 22 minutes and any change in the app locks the database resources. Propose and start to implement a split into three stacks: infra/stacks/network, infra/stacks/data, and infra/stacks/app.
Start by listing every resource address in the current plan output saved in infra/root/plan-2026-11-01.txt and assign each to one of the three stacks. Resources that reference each other across stacks must use terraform_remote_state data sources, not copied values.
Do not run terraform state mv, terraform apply, or any command that changes a remote state. Only write files. Put the moved resource blocks in the new folders and leave a short README.md in each stack explaining the state key.
Context: the platform team asked that no state key changes its name during the split, because the CI jobs read the keys from a shared variable file. Keep the key names in the design unchanged.
Report back: the resource address mapping as a table, the list of cross-stack references, and any resource you could not place with the reason. Also state the migration steps that a human must run, one per line, without running them.

Pick serializer for event bus
The event bus needs a serializer for 2 KB messages. Read libs/events/src/codec and docs/adr/0021-codec.md. Name the best option and one risk. Keep it under twelve lines.

Trace lost webhook events
Some webhook events never reach the handler in hooks/receiver.py. Check retry semantics and the timing of the 200 response. Identify the root cause in logs/hooks_2026-11-02.log.

Ambiguous: make search feel faster
The product owner asked us to make search feel faster on the storefront. Nobody defined faster. The search endpoint is in services/search and the front end is in apps/storefront/src/search. Investigate what the user would actually notice, for example first results, typing lag, or full page reload. Read the code paths for the first keystroke and the response rendering. Propose three measurable definitions of faster, each with a metric you can collect from the browser or from server logs. Do not change code. Report under thirty lines.

Design CLI plugin architecture
Propose a plugin architecture for packages/cli so third parties can add subcommands without forking. Constraints: plugins are npm packages named cli-plugin-*, they load from a config list, core command startup must stay within 30 ms more, and plugin versions must be pinned. Write a design doc at docs/design/cli-plugins.md with the loading strategy, manifest format, error isolation, security concerns, and a three-phase rollout. Do not implement. Report the doc path and the open questions you could not resolve.

Design rollback for migration tool
The migration tool in tools/migrator applies SQL files forward only. Ops wants a rollback command that undoes the last applied migration safely. Some migrations contain data changes that cannot be reversed by a plain down file.

Read tools/migrator/main.go, tools/migrator/store.go and the file list in db/migrations/. Count how many existing migration files have a down file. Design a rollback command that refuses to run when the migration has no down file or is marked irreversible. Write the design in docs/design/migrator-rollback.md with the command syntax, the state table changes and the failure cases.

Report back: the count of migrations with and without down files, the design summary, and the failure cases you covered. Do not change the tool code.

Design plugin system for exporters
Design a plugin system so third parties can add new export formats to the reporting service in reporting/. Today each format is a hard-coded class in reporting/formats/. Propose the discovery mechanism, the interface, how versions are checked and how a broken plugin is isolated. Compare entry points against a plain directory scan. Output a design doc of at most 80 lines in docs/design/exporter_plugins.md. Do not implement any code yet.

Review upload handler security
Review services/files/src/routes/upload.ts for security problems. The route accepts multipart uploads, stores files under UPLOAD_DIR using the original filename, and returns a public URL. Check path traversal, trust in content-type, size limits, and whether the public URL exposes other users' files. List each issue with severity and line number. Do not change code. Report the three most serious issues first.

Choose audit log storage design
Choose between Postgres JSONB column and a separate events table for the audit log. Use query patterns in docs/audit_queries.md. Give a recommendation with trade-offs in ten lines or fewer.

Decide public API versioning scheme
The public API currently has no version scheme. Clients use the paths /orders and /invoices. Product wants to ship breaking changes to the response shape of orders later this quarter. Mobile clients update slowly. Partners asked for a deprecation window of six months.

Compare three options: a path prefix such as /v2, a header such as API-Version, and a media type with a version parameter. Use the access log summary in ops/api/clients-2026-10.csv to estimate how many clients use each path. Recommend one option and describe the deprecation steps. Note what you could not determine from the data.

Report back: the recommendation, the client count per path from the CSV, the deprecation timeline, and the unknowns. Write nothing under services/.

Plan migration from Celery to queue service
The notifications team wants to replace Celery with a managed queue service for the notification pipeline in C:/work/notify. Today the pipeline uses Celery tasks in notify/tasks.py, a Redis broker, and beat schedules in config/beat.py. About 40 tasks are involved, and they run about 1.8 million jobs per day. Several tasks use chords and chains, and two tasks use countdown and eta to schedule future work.

Task: write a migration plan. Read notify/tasks.py, config/beat.py and docs/notify/architecture.md. List every task, its trigger, whether it uses chord, chain, eta, countdown or retries, and whether it is idempotent. Identify the tasks that are hard to migrate, meaning those with chords, eta-based scheduling or shared locks. Propose how each category of task would move, and whether a dual-run phase is safe for each category.

Address ordering guarantees. Celery does not promise order across tasks, but some consumers rely on order for the same customer id. Check docs/notify/architecture.md for any ordering promise and check the consumers in notify/consumers.py.

Address the failure modes: a message delivered twice during the switch, a message lost during the switch, and a beat schedule that fires on both systems during the transition. Propose a verification approach for each.

Constraints: do not change any code or configuration in this task. Do not contact the managed queue vendor. Do not read the production broker state.

Deliver the plan as a markdown file at docs/plans/celery_to_queue.md, at most 150 lines, with a table of tasks and a phased rollout. Include a rollback path for each phase.

Report back: the file path, the count of tasks in each migration category, the top three risks, and the one decision that the team must make before any work starts. Keep the report under 30 lines.

Investigate ingest memory growth
The ingest worker RSS grows about 40 MB per hour under a steady load of 200 messages per second. Use perf/heaptrack-ingest.zst if it exists. If it does not exist, propose a measurement method and stop. Report the top three allocation sites and the likely leak.

Root-cause flaky login test
The Playwright login spec fails about 1 in 6 runs on CI with 'element detached'. Find the cause in e2e/login.spec.ts and src/auth/LoginForm.tsx. Propose a fix but do not apply it. Report the root cause with file:line.

Find deadlock in migration runner
The SQL Server migration runner in tools/dbmigrate sometimes deadlocks when two pods start at the same time. Find the root cause in the lock acquisition code in Locking.cs and in the SchemaHistory table writes. Do not change the schema of SchemaHistory. Report the deadlock graph source lines and a fix proposal in under fifteen lines.

Explain race in like button
Two rapid clicks on Like make the count flip back. Analyze src/hooks/useLike.ts with the react-query mutation. Find the race and explain it in under 10 lines.

Find goroutine leak in HTTP client pool
The Go service in services/gateway-go shows a goroutine count rising from about 400 to 9000 over 24 hours in production. The pprof goroutine profile from the staging soak test is saved in .agent/data/goroutines-staging.txt. Use it as the starting evidence. Do not run a new production profile.
The service builds an HTTP client pool in internal/upstream/pool.go and uses a context per request in internal/upstream/call.go. The retry loop is in internal/upstream/retry.go. Start by grouping the goroutines in the saved profile by their top frame and by the first application frame, and count each group. Record the top three groups with the file and line numbers that appear in the stacks.
Check for these common causes: a response body that is not closed on the error path, a goroutine that waits on a channel nobody reads after the context is cancelled, a time.After in a loop, and a select that has no case for ctx.Done(). Use grep for Body.Close, time.After, and ctx.Done across internal/upstream to check each pattern.
If you can run the unit tests with go test -race ./internal/upstream/..., do so and record any race warning. Do not run the soak test.
Report back with: the top three goroutine groups with counts, the stack frames that point at application code, each pattern check result with its file and line, the race test result, and the most likely leak with the evidence that supports it. Do not change any code.

Design config reload without restart
Design how services/billing-api reloads feature flags without a restart. Write docs/design/flag-reload.md covering the source of truth, the consistency model and the rollback path. List open questions at the end of the file.

Plan migration from XML to YAML config
The Java service inventory-api reads its settings from a 900-line XML file config/app.xml. The team wants YAML with the same keys and the same override rules from environment variables. Design the migration. Read the loader in src/main/java/com/example/inventory/config/ConfigLoader.java and list the override rules it implements. Propose a plan with the order of steps, the compatibility period, and the test that proves both formats produce the same object. Do not write code. Keep the plan under forty lines.

Explain flaky date test in CI
The test tests/test_invoices.py::test_due_date_end_of_month fails only in CI and only between 23:00 and 01:00 UTC. Locally it always passes. Study the helper due_date() in billing/dates.py, the freeze_time usage in tests/conftest.py and the TZ setting in the CI config at .github/workflows/test.yml. Explain the root cause and give the exact line where the bug lives.

Find render regression in inbox
After the last release the Inbox list takes 300 ms longer to render with 5k items. Profile src/features/inbox and find the cause. Report the cause and a measured before and after number.

Consolidate retry logic across services
Five Java services in the monorepo each implement their own retry loop for calls to the pricing API. The loops differ in backoff, jitter, and which HTTP status codes they retry. The services are catalog, cart, checkout, search-indexer, and promotions.
Find each retry loop with grep for the word retry and for the class name PricingClient in each service. Create a table with the service, the file, the max attempts, the backoff, the jitter, and the retried status codes.
Decide whether one shared RetryPolicy class in the module platform-http is safe. For each service, state whether its current behavior must be kept. Do not change any behavior that a test depends on.
Write the new shared class and migrate only the catalog service in this run, keeping its tests green. Leave the other four services unchanged and list them as the next steps.
Run ./gradlew :catalog:test :platform-http:test and report the summary.
Context: the pricing API returns 409 for a stale price version, and the catalog service treats 409 as a retry case while the other services do not. Keep that difference visible in the table and do not merge it silently.
Report back: the table, the list of behaviors that differ and must be kept, the test result, and the four remaining services with their known blockers.

Bump pinned Python dev tools
The file requirements-dev.txt of the data-pipeline repo pins black, ruff, and mypy. The team agreed to upgrade only the patch versions for these three tools in this change. Check the current versions in the file first.

Change the pin for black from the current version to the next patch version available in the pip index, and do the same for ruff and mypy. Use pip index versions black, pip index versions ruff, and pip index versions mypy to find the latest patch release in the current minor series.

Do not change any runtime requirement in requirements.txt. Do not change the minor version of any tool. If the latest patch in the current series is the same as the pin, leave that line unchanged and say so.

Run pip install -r requirements-dev.txt --dry-run to check the resolution, then run black --check src and ruff check src and report the exit codes. Do not run mypy over the whole repository because it takes over twenty minutes; run mypy only on src/pipeline/core.py.

Pytest fixture for database sessions
Add a pytest fixture module at services/ledger-py/tests/conftest_db.py that provides a SQLAlchemy session bound to a per-test transaction that is rolled back at the end of each test. The database is PostgreSQL in the test container named by the environment variable LEDGER_TEST_DATABASE_URL. If the variable is not set, the fixture skips the test with the message LEDGER_TEST_DATABASE_URL not set, and does not fail.
Pattern: open a connection, begin an outer transaction, bind the session to that connection with join_transaction_mode set to create_savepoint, and roll back the outer transaction after yield. Make the fixture function-scoped. Do not use the global engine from app/db.py; create a new engine inside the fixture factory so the test engine stays isolated.
Add a helper function make_session_factory(url: str) returning the sessionmaker, and keep it in the same module so tests can import it directly.
Write one smoke test in services/ledger-py/tests/test_db_fixture.py that inserts a row into the table accounts and asserts it is visible within the test, then add a second test that asserts the row is not visible, which proves the rollback. Use two tests with the same unique account code so the order of execution does not matter.
Run LEDGER_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset first and run python -m pytest services/ledger-py/tests/test_db_fixture.py -q, and report the summary, which must show skips. Then run it with the local URL from docs/local-db.md and report the summary.
Report back with the files changed, both pytest summary lines, and whether the second smoke test passed with the rollback in place.

Change Makefile lint target flags
Context: the Makefile at the root of the analytics service runs the lint target with flake8, but the team switched to ruff last month. The current lint target runs flake8 with the flag --max-line-length 100 and a directory list. We need the lint target to run ruff check with the same directory list and the same max line length. The format target already uses ruff format and should not change.

Steps: open Makefile and find the lint target. Note its exact lines, including tabs. Make sure every recipe line in the target still starts with a literal tab character and not spaces; GNU make fails otherwise. Replace the flake8 command with ruff check --line-length 100 followed by the same directory list. Keep the echo line above it if one exists. Do not edit other targets. Remove flake8 from the lint target only, not from requirements files.

Constraints: the top-level variable LINT_DIRS must stay the same value. Do not add new variables. Do not rename the target. If the target has a dependency on a target named install-flake8, leave that dependency in place and report it, because another target may use it.

Verification: run make -n lint from the repo root and paste the output, which must show ruff check and not flake8. Run make lint and paste the last ten lines of output and the exit code. If ruff is not installed in this environment, the make lint command will fail with command not found. In that case report the failure and do not install ruff.

Report back: the old recipe line, the new recipe line, the make -n output, the make lint exit code, and any other target that refers to flake8. Keep the report under 20 lines.

Update CHANGELOG compare links
The CHANGELOG.md file at the repo root uses compare links at the bottom of the file for each released version, in the form [1.4.0]: https://github.com/example-org/acme-widgets/compare/v1.3.2...v1.4.0. Update logback pattern in config
The logging configuration file src/main/resources/logback.xml of the Spring service support-gateway uses the pattern %d{HH:mm:ss} for the timestamp. The team wants the ISO format with the date, so the new pattern is %d{yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSXXX}.

Change the pattern only in the appender named CONSOLE. Do not change the pattern in the appender named FILE, because the log shipper parses that one with a fixed regex. Do not change the levels or the logger names.

Check the XML is still well formed with xmllint --noout src/main/resources/logback.xml. Then start no application. Instead run ./gradlew :support-gateway:test --tests '*LoggingConfig*' if that test exists, and report the result.

If the test LoggingConfigTest does not exist, say so and do not create it. Report the grep -n pattern src/main/resources/logback.xml output after the change.

Context: the log shipper that reads the CONSOLE output in the staging pods expects the timestamp with a fixed width. Mention in the report if the new pattern changes the width of the timestamp field compared with the old one.
Report back: the output of the grep, the xmllint result, and the test result or the note that no test exists.

Next.js middleware for locale redirect
Add locale detection to middleware.ts at the root of apps/marketing. Requests to paths without a locale prefix should redirect to the best locale. Supported locales are en, de, and fr, with en as default. The matcher must exclude /_next, /api, static files with an extension, and the path /robots.txt.
Detection order: first the cookie named NEXT_LOCALE if its value is a supported locale. Second, the Accept-Language header, where you pick the first supported language tag by quality value; ignore tags below quality 0.5. If nothing matches, use en. Redirect with a 307 status so the decision is not cached permanently.
Do not redirect a request whose path already starts with a supported locale, and do not redirect the root path of a locale, such as /de, since that is already a valid page.
Write the parsing logic in apps/marketing/lib/locale.ts as a pure function pickLocale(cookieValue: string | undefined, acceptLanguage: string | null): 'en' | 'de' | 'fr'. Keep the middleware file itself thin, calling pickLocale.
Tests: add apps/marketing/__tests__/locale.test.ts that covers the cookie win, the Accept-Language quality ordering, the quality value below 0.5 being ignored, an unsupported language falling back to en, and a null header. Do not test the middleware runtime here.
Run npm test --workspace apps/marketing -- locale and report the summary. Run npx next lint --dir middleware.ts --dir lib and report the exit code.
Report back with the files changed, the test summary line, the lint exit code, and the pickLocale output for the header value de-CH;q=0.9,fr;q=0.8 with no cookie.

Pin Node version in web CI
In .github/workflows/web-ci.yml change node-version from 18 to 20 in both the build job and the lint job. Also write the value 20 into the file .nvmrc at the repo root, with no trailing text.
Keep the YAML indentation and quoting style of the file. Do not change the cache key or the runner image.
Validate the workflow with actionlint if it is installed, otherwise run yamllint on that one file.
Report back: the two changed files and the validator result in one line.

Cursor pagination for orders list
Add cursor-based pagination to GET /api/orders in services/orders/src/routes/orders.ts. Query params: cursor, an opaque base64 string of created_at and id, and limit, default 25, max 100. The response shape becomes { items, nextCursor }, where nextCursor is null on the last page. Update listOrders in services/orders/src/repo/orders.ts to accept the cursor. Bulk upsert with chunking in store
Context: the sync job in services/ledger-sync writes about 400,000 rows per night one at a time, which takes 3 hours. Add a bulk upsert method that writes rows in chunks, using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Keep the existing single-row method for the API path.

Requirements:
1. Add func (s *Store) UpsertMany(ctx context.Context, rows []Entry) (int, error). It writes all rows and returns the number of rows affected.

Constraints:
- Do not change the schema or add a migration.
- Do not change Upsert.
- Use the database/sql API already used in entries.go. Do not add pgx-specific calls.
- Keep the chunk size as a constant named upsertChunkSize, unexported.
